tier_reason: Independent third-party suite (ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark, a fork of Mozilla arewefastyet's v8-v7 benchmarks, run daily by .github/workflows/update.yml) shows lo's total score above Node 26.10.0 on all three platforms; the benchmark code is public but compiler/flags of the prebuilt binaries and runner CPU models are not stated, so not A.

corrections.caveats: lo's own README makes no performance claim; the evidence is only the third-party daily table (snapshot of 2026-10-05, lo 0.0.33.pre, Node 26.10.0 via setup-node 'latest'; prebuilt stripped binaries installed by ahaoboy/js-engine-setup), which is regenerated every day so the numbers drift. Because lo embeds V8, the gap to Node reflects V8 version, flags and heap/runtime setup rather than a new engine: the largest per-test gaps are on GC-heavy Splay (macOS 49432 vs 15574, windows 35017 vs 13056), on windows lo trails Node on Richards (32563 vs 34370) and DeltaBlue (71216 vs 74561), and plain V8 d8 scores higher than lo on every platform (ubuntu 48107, macOS arm64 64220, windows 46932). The v8-v7 suite is old, each platform is one CI run per day, and hardware is whatever the GitHub runner provides.

notes: All six scores in claimed_speedup match the ubuntu, macos-arm64 and windows Score rows of the README table dated 10/5/2026, and lo is above Bun and Deno on all three (windows margin over Deno is small: 40191 vs 39991). Shortcomings: win over Node is a V8 embedding/config effect, not an engine; d8 itself beats lo everywhere; daily single CI runs on unspecified runner CPUs. Metadata checked: MIT, 390 stars, last commit 2026-09-16.

tier_reason: First-party numbers only: one aobench bar chart (aobench.png) in the README; the harness tests/benchmarks/bench.py (hyperfine, lightstorm binary vs the same program as mruby bytecode) and clang-19 presets are public, but no CPU model, run count or exact build configuration is tied to the chart.

corrections.baseline: mruby VM executing the same program's precompiled bytecode (tests/benchmarks/bench.py pairs 'lightstorm <bench>' with 'mruby <bench>' built from mrbc bytecode linked to mruby_static); the README chart labels it only 'Baseline'
corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'The compiled version (rightmost) decreases total execution time by nearly ~30%'. Reading the aobench.png bar chart: time about 78% of baseline for Compiled and about 71% for Compiled + escape + CSE (about 1.4x faster, derived from page data); the bar labelled 'Misses' (type not stated) is about 47% and 43% of baseline (values read off the chart).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: CMakePresets.json: CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release with clang-19/clang++-19 on Ubuntu (Homebrew llvm@19 on macOS); LIGHTSTORM_CFLAGS for generated C is -g by default and -g -flto -O3 only when LIGHTSTORM_LTO is set; the mruby bytecode baseline executables add -g. Which configuration produced the chart is not stated.
corrections.caveats: One benchmark (aobench, tests/benchmarks/bm_ao_render.rb) and the numbers exist only in a PNG chart; the baseline is mruby's bytecode VM (not CRuby MRI or YJIT), confirmed from tests/benchmarks/bench.py although the README does not name it; no hardware, run count or build configuration is given for the chart; the LLVM blog post with more detail (blog.llvm.org/posts/2024-12-03-minimalistic-ruby-compiler) could not be opened here (egress blocked); last commit December 2024.

notes: Chart values in the record are read correctly (78% and 71% time); the inferred mruby baseline is confirmed by bench.py, which times lightstorm vs mruby bytecode with hyperfine. Shortcomings: single benchmark shown, chart only, no hardware or run details, stale since 2024-12-13, and only about 1.4x vs an interpreter. Metadata checked: MIT, 143 stars, last commit 2024-12-13 (stale).

tier_reason: First-party README table produced by the repo's own harness (benchmarks/run_benchmarks.py with benchmark_comprehensive.mob/.lua/.py, checksum-verified medians of five runs); release flags are in buildy.yaml but CPU model, Lua build and CPython version are not stated, so not A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: buildy.yaml release configuration: -O3 -march=native -funroll-loops -flto with -flto -Wl,-O1 at link on Linux (macOS: -O3 -funroll-loops -flto); run_benchmarks.py picks bin/mobius or build/linux-x86_64-release/bin/mobius. Which build produced the README table is not stated.
corrections.caveats: The committed raw results (benchmarks/benchmark_summary_latest.json and benchmark_comprehensive_*_latest.txt, last changed 2026-07-12 in commit 7f9a92c) show Mobius totalling 0.547 s vs Lua 0.420 s (about 1.3x slower than Lua) and CPython 1.419 s (about 2.6x faster) (derived from page data). They predate the README table: the 2026-07-13 and 2026-07-14 commits added intrinsic opcodes and small-string pools (commit 4fdf039 reports 431 ms vs Lua 455 ms), slimmer call frames, table and array op fusions, added type annotations to the Mobius fib benchmark only (f32cde8), and changed the Mobius mixed workload from data:get(i) to data[i] (29a409c). So the README's Lua win is newer than the committed JSON rather than contradicted by it, but the raw output behind the README table is not committed. The Mobius fib script uses typed parameters that the Lua and Python scripts cannot express. Hardware, Lua build (run_benchmarks.py uses whatever 'lua' or 'lua5.4' is on PATH) and CPython version are not stated. Micro-benchmarks only; Mobius is slower than Lua on fib, dense arrays and string-key tables and slower than CPython on string ops, object create/destroy and the mixed workload; version 0.1.0, 3 stars.

notes: README table numbers match the record exactly (373.9 vs Lua 443.3 vs CPython 1424.8 ms). The search agent's contradiction is real but explained by timing: the committed benchmark_summary_latest.json (1.30x slower than Lua) is from 2026-07-12, before the 2026-07-13/14 optimization and benchmark-script commits that the README table reflects; record as shortcoming 'README Lua win not backed by committed raw results; committed results are stale and show Mobius 1.3x slower than Lua'.
